chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).

Regarding a man who confessed upon himself that he had taken possession of a slave girl of a man, so the slave girl gave birth from the possessor. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The slave girl and the child are returned to the one from whom she was taken, when the possessor has confessed with that.'

key_terms.الْغَاصِب: The possessor / The one who took possession
key_terms.الْمَغْصُوب مِنْهُ: The one from whom the property was taken (original owner)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave girl and her child if the possessor confesses to taking her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'Umd al-Dam' (confession) in property law, establishing that a possessor's admission of usurpation (ghasb) is sufficient to restore both the slave girl and her offspring to the original owner. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the child's status follows the mother, ensuring the continuity of ownership rights even after the transfer of possession through usurpation.
